area: tools/ — the 56 harness directories, tools/run-tests.sh, tools/lib/, and the CI gate that consumes them
summary:
GATE MAP. 56 dirs; 54 have a run.sh (lib/ and release/ are helpers). `run-tests.sh:70-89` gates 41 in `scientific` (CI runs this plus `unit` on every push, .github/workflows/ci.yml:100-133); `all` adds `real-data-acceptance` + `package-test` (run-tests.sh:101) = 43 today. Eleven are ungated: acom-groundtruth, bragg-spacing-probe, origin-fit-diagnostics, performance-baseline, real-acom-benchmark, residency-sweep, stage-tb1-ws2-fixture, training-dataset-campaign, ui-qc-playthrough, ui-smoke-test, volume-mmap-probe. Genuinely protected: every Core/Data reader and LoadSpecification path, the disk/probe/FFT/correlation stack, the EMD writer and sidecar, strain (incl. the S8 frame), parallax (all five stages), the crystal model, and the three .metal-compiling harnesses that keep all 8 shaders building. Genuinely unprotected: Core/Analysis/RotationCalibration.swift and PtychographyPreparation.swift (zero gated harness, zero unit test — PtychographyPreparation additionally has no callers at all), the `centerOfMass` kernel's parameter block, and the concurrent disk path this area's own README claims to guard.

WHAT THIS AREA DOES WELL, and it is a lot. Anti-vacuity is a live discipline, not a slogan: strain-frame-test/main.swift:172 asserts `compared > 50` so a masked loop cannot pass empty; preprocess-crop-bin-test:90-91 and two-spec-analysis-test:377-380 always `check(false, …)` BEFORE they `continue`; load-spec-roundtrip:202 carries an explicit `else { check(false, …) }`. ws2-crystal-test/main.swift:185-263 ships four negative controls that each fail loudly if they cannot see their own mutation, and its header (11-19) states exactly which error classes it cannot catch. q-calibration-gate-test/main.swift:1-23 opens by telling the reader 26 of 32 mutations leave it green. sources.manifest exists because a hand-spelled list broke 5 of 8 harnesses, and it exits 66 on a missing path (lib/sources.manifest:238-246). strain-frame-test/reference.py:52-70 and preprocess-crop-bin-test/reference.py:22-31 pin literal expressions in the vendored py4DSTEM source and refuse to run without it. Every one of the 54 runners sets `set -e`; 52 also set `pipefail`, and no pipeline in the gated set can swallow a failure. No harness uses `assert()` (which -O would strip). Ground truth is honest about itself where it comes from the app: disk-correlation-parity/main.swift:2-19, virtual-detector-residency/run.sh:2-4 and ws2-crystal-test/main.swift:132-141 all say so in the file. KNOWN ITEMS I FOUND AND AM NOT RE-REPORTING: real-data-acceptance's empty-glob SKIP exiting 0 (run.sh:42-45), acom-groundtruth ungated / OrientationPlan.project blind to every ACOM harness, bragg-spacing-probe and residency-sweep gating nothing, real-data-acceptance hand-spelling 18 sources instead of the manifest, q-calibration-gate-test's 26/32 mutation survivors, and the owed mac4DSTEMUITests/ui-qc-playthrough deletion — all already in docs/open-items.md.

findings.title: Gated parity-metric check is a tautology: it compares an expression against a byte-identical recomputation of itself
findings.why: Line 85 builds `round_tripped = B @ P`; line 86 then calls `misorientation_deg(round_tripped, np.einsum("nij,jk->nik", B, P), SYM)` — the second argument is the same expression recomputed, not an independent quantity. `misorientation_deg` (parity_py4dstem.py:310-317) forms `A @ B.T` and minimises the angle over the symmetry group, so for X orthogonal it returns exactly 0 for X-against-X and the identity operator is always in SYM. The check is therefore already fully subsumed by line 45-47 ("a matrix has zero misorientation with itself") and cannot discriminate any value of the lab-frame map P at line 27. The comment at 83-84 claims it verifies that "an app matrix that is exactly py4DSTEM's answer must score zero", which would require comparing a frame-mapped app matrix against py4DSTEM's B — no app-side and py4DSTEM-side pair is ever brought together here. This harness is gated (`parity-metric-test`, run-tests.sh:74) and is the *only* thing fact-checking the comparator that produces the ACOM parity numbers, so CI reports a passing check that tests nothing. This is precisely the repo's named failure mode: an assertion that cannot fail.
findings.failureScenario: Set `P` at test_parity_metric.py:27 to its own transpose — [[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,-1]] transposed is a different proper rotation than the one parity_py4dstem.py:427 applies. The line 65 sensitivity check still passes (drift is still > 1 deg, it only requires that SOME lab-frame change is visible) and the line 87 round-trip check still passes (it is X vs X). The suite prints "all metric checks passed", exit 0, CI green — while the comparator maps py4DSTEM's orientation matrices into the wrong lab frame and every reported misorientation on a multi-grain dataset is wrong.

findings.title: load-spec-roundtrip's "real claim" block is skipped silently when both LoadView constructions throw
findings.why: Lines 79-80 use `try?`, so a throwing `LoadView.init` yields nil rather than a failure. The only assertion on that outcome is line 81-82, `check((before == nil) == (after == nil))`, which is satisfied when BOTH are nil. Everything the file's own header (lines 11-18) calls the real claim — section 2's shape / read-crop / edge-trim comparison and section 3's entire calibration re-reference block, lines 84-135 — lives inside `if let before, let after` and evaporates with no record. The harness then reaches line 210 and prints "load-spec-roundtrip: all passed", exit 0. The omission is demonstrably inconsistent rather than deliberate: the same file handles the analogous nil case correctly 100 lines later at 189/202-204 (`if let recipeJSON … } else { check(false, "a non-empty replay record failed to encode") }`), and sibling harnesses guard the same shape explicitly (strain-frame-test/main.swift:172 asserts `compared > 50`).
findings.failureScenario: Tighten a bound in `LoadView.init` (or change the harness's `source` shape at main.swift:33-38) so that all four non-full-extent specifications at lines 41-54 are rejected. `before` and `after` are both nil for every case, line 81's symmetry check passes, sections 2 and 3 never execute, and the gate certifies that a load specification survives the sidecar and re-applies to the source with identical calibration — while in fact zero specifications were applied and zero calibration values were compared.

findings.title: disk-correlation-parity's README claims the gate guards the concurrent path; the gated invocation never runs it, and the harness's parallel branch does not mirror the production work split
findings.why: README.md:13 says "Part of `tools/run-tests.sh scientific`" and README.md:19-23, under "## What it guards", asserts "**The concurrent path agrees with the serial one.** `--backend cpu-parallel` mirrors `DiskDetection.detectAll` … A data race or a work-splitting bug in the parallel detector shows up as a checksum mismatch." Neither half holds. (a) `run-tests.sh:76` invokes the harness with no arguments, `run.sh:39` forwards an empty `"$@"`, and `main.swift:153` defaults `var backend = "cpu"` — so under every gate, and under CI, only the single-threaded loop runs. (b) Even a manual `--backend cpu-parallel` does not exercise the production split: `main.swift:239` strides individual *patterns* across workers (`stride(from: w, to: patterns.count, by: workers)`) and calls `det.detectWithDiagnostics`, while production `DiskDetection.detectAll` strides scan *rows* (`DiskDetection.swift:869`, `stride(from: w, to: d.ry, by: workers)`) and calls `det.detect`. The harness re-implements a different splitter and checks its own copy. Related: `main.swift:341` validates `baseline.patternCount` and `baseline.detector` but never `baseline.backend`, so a baseline recorded under one backend is silently compared against a run under the other. This violates the repo's hard rule that no claim may stand which a reader cannot reproduce.
findings.failureScenario: Introduce shared mutable state in `DiskDetector` (or an off-by-one in the row stride at DiskDetection.swift:869 that skips the last worker's rows). `run-tests.sh scientific` and CI stay green: the gated run only executes the serial loop at main.swift:265+, and even the parallel branch strides patterns, not rows, so it never touches the changed splitter. The app — which calls `detectAll` from AppState.swift:4646 — silently drops or duplicates scan rows of Bragg peaks, and every downstream strain and ACOM number is computed from an incomplete peak set.

findings.title: CoMParams is the one Metal parameter struct with no independent arbiter — its only check compares the kernel against itself
findings.why: CLAUDE.md makes it a hard rule that Metal parameter structs in MetalEngine.swift stay byte-for-byte identical to the matching .metal structs, because a mismatch is silent corruption. Two of the three are actually gated against something independent: `ApertureParams` through `VirtualDetector.run` at virtual-detector-test/main.swift:135-137, compared to `test.expected` generated by reference.py; `OriginParams` through two-spec-analysis-test/main.swift:886-923, compared to origins the fixture planted and wrote to origins.txt. `CoMParams` is not. Its only exercise in all of tools/ and mac4DSTEMTests/ (verified by grep for `centerOfMass` and `CoMParams`) is virtual-detector-test/main.swift:169-178, which compares `MetalEngine.shared.centerOfMass` against `VirtualDetector.tiledCenterOfMass` — and the tiled path builds the same `CoMParams` at VirtualDetector.swift:446-450 and calls the same `MetalEngine.centerOfMass` at :452. Both operands are produced by the same kernel through the same parameter block, so a layout divergence at or after the `cx` field (MetalEngine.swift:54 vs CenterOfMass.metal:23) shifts both sides identically and the exact comparison still passes. MetalEngine.swift:320 pushes `MemoryLayout<CoMParams>.stride` of the SWIFT struct, which is what makes the two definitions load-bearing.
findings.failureScenario: Add a field to CenterOfMass.metal's struct (say `uint flags;` after `qx` at line 22) without adding it to MetalEngine.swift:49-57 — the shape mutation the hard rule exists to prevent. The kernel then reads Swift's `cx` bits as `flags`, `cy` as `cx`, `useOrigins` as `cy`, and garbage as `useOrigins`. virtual-detector-test's line 178 comparison is still bit-exact because resident and tiled paths are corrupted identically, so `scientific` and CI are green; the app's DPC/iDPC center-of-mass field is measured against a nonsense reference centre and every CoM shift, and the R-Q rotation solved from it, is wrong.

findings.title: RotationCalibration — a py4DSTEM port with its own DEVIATION, feeding iDPC and parallax — has zero coverage in any gate
findings.why: Core/Analysis/RotationCalibration.swift is an explicit port of py4DSTEM's `_solve_for_center_of_mass_relative_rotation` (header lines 5-6) and carries an inline DEVIATION at lines 16-18 (a 0.1 deg refinement pass py4DSTEM does not perform). Its output — `rotationRad` and the `transpose` flag — is stored on AppState.swift:343, computed at AppState.swift:4214, displayed to the user via DatasetInspector.swift:493-496, and consumed as `calibration.rotationRad` / `transposeQR` by ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:47-88, i.e. it sets the frame for every parallax and ptychography result. The only file in the repository that compiles it is tools/training-dataset-campaign/run.sh:32, and that harness appears in no array in run-tests.sh (it needs gitignored multi-GB cubes and SKIPs at run.sh:50). Nothing under mac4DSTEMTests/ mentions it (grep returns nothing). So a py4DSTEM-ported scientific solver with a declared deviation is protected by neither Track A gate. The same is true of Core/Analysis/PtychographyPreparation.swift, which additionally has no callers anywhere — the gated `singleslice-ptychography-test` pins the reconstruction engine while the only bridge from app data into it is uncovered and unwired.
findings.failureScenario: Flip a sign in the curl computation or invert the transpose branch in RotationCalibration.solve. `run-tests.sh unit`, `run-tests.sh scientific` and CI are all green — no compiled harness and no XCTest touches the file. The app then reports an R-Q rotation off by the transpose (or by 90 deg), the parallax stack rotates the CoM field into the wrong frame from ParallaxPreprocessing.swift:80-88 onward, and iDPC contrast and every parallax depth section are quantitatively wrong with no gate anywhere that can notice.

findings.title: README's public, reproducible harness count went stale when ws2-crystal-test joined the gate
findings.why: README.md:40 states "`tools/run-tests.sh all` — **exit 0 over 42 harnesses** … That aggregate is 40 scientific harnesses … plus real-data acceptance and packaging", presented as what "anyone with the repository can reproduce". The `scientific` array at run-tests.sh:70-89 now contains 41 entries (counted mechanically), because `ws2-crystal-test` was added at line 78 in commit 81893fb (W4a, 2026-08-31); README was last touched in f4495aa (M2), which precedes it. `all` (run-tests.sh:101) therefore starts 43 harnesses today, not 42. CLAUDE.md's own instruction — "Do not quote a harness count from memory — run-tests.sh is the only thing that knows it" — records that this exact drift already happened once ("it was 39 at the S13 closeout and the docs said 38 for three days after that"), and the repo hard rule is that no claim may stand which a reader cannot reproduce. docs/v2-release.md:754 has the correct 41/41 figure for the W4a run, so the two documents now disagree.
findings.failureScenario: A reader clones the public repo, runs `tools/run-tests.sh all`, counts 43 `==> name` lines against the README's advertised 42, and cannot tell whether they are looking at documentation drift or at a harness that ran twice. On a public GPL release the aggregate claim is the credibility of the whole gate.

findings.title: sources.manifest's "STATUS, STATED PLAINLY" understates adoption by three times
findings.why: Lines 31-36 say: "STATUS, STATED PLAINLY: tools/two-spec-analysis-test and tools/strain-frame-test (v2 S8) source this file today. The hand-listing runners are exactly as exposed to the 2026-08-17 failure as they were before it existed." Six runners source it now — `grep -ln sources.manifest tools/*/run.sh` returns origin-fit-diagnostics, reduced-export-test, q-calibration-gate-test, two-spec-analysis-test, strain-frame-test and ws2-crystal-test. The paragraph is emphatic precisely because it was written to be trusted ("saying otherwise would be a claim a reader cannot reproduce"), and this file is the repo's single maintained source-list authority, so a stale self-description here is the highest-leverage kind. Migration is governed by docs/development-process.md §1 ("when next touched"), which makes progress invisible unless the status line is kept current.
findings.failureScenario: A session adds a Core/Data file, reads lines 31-36, concludes that only two harnesses are manifest-driven, and hand-edits the other runners' source lists — re-creating the 2026-08-17 breakage in the four harnesses that would have been fixed for free by adding one line to a group here. Or the inverse: it audits the "hand-listing runners" and skips q-calibration-gate-test and ws2-crystal-test as already covered when they are not.

findings.title: CI's exclusion list promises completeness but omits three ungated harnesses added the day after it was written
findings.why: Line 14-15 states the rule for this block: "WHAT IS EXCLUDED, AND WHY — silence is never the reason something is missing (docs/v2-release.md §3)". Lines 16-31 then enumerate real-data-acceptance, package-test, bragg-spacing-probe, residency-sweep, real-acom-benchmark, training-dataset-campaign, acom-groundtruth, ui-smoke-test, ui-qc-playthrough + mac4DSTEMUITests, `benchmark`, and Track B. Three harness directories with a run.sh are absent from both the gate and the list: tools/origin-fit-diagnostics, tools/volume-mmap-probe and tools/stage-tb1-ws2-fixture (grep for all three in ci.yml returns 0 hits). ci.yml was last committed in 2532d35 (S17, 2026-08-27); all three landed 2026-08-28 (185d9bb, c45bac3, 1888b15), so the list went stale three times without anyone updating it, against CLAUDE.md's "Keep docs current as part of 'done'". origin-fit-diagnostics matters most: docs/open-items.md:543 and :1742 cite its measurements as S12 evidence, so a reader can reasonably assume it is exercised.
findings.failureScenario: A reviewer checking whether the CI gate covers the origin-fit residual work reads the exclusion list, finds origin-fit-diagnostics absent from it, and — trusting the file's own 'silence is never the reason' guarantee — concludes it must be inside the `scientific` array. It is not (run-tests.sh:70-89), so the S12 evidence tool has never run in CI and its numbers are only as fresh as the last hand-run.
